description: Curated FDA clearances and approvals with the actual study designs FDA accepted. Used to ground regulatory section claims in verified precedents rather than LLM training-data defaults. Sources: FDA 510(k) database, De Novo database, PMA database, Drugs@FDA, published FDA decision summaries.

clearances.indication: Autonomous AI detection of diabetic retinopathy in primary care settings
clearances.trial_design: Prospective pivotal study at 10 US primary care sites
primary_endpoints: Sensitivity ≥85.0% vs. dilated fundus exam gold standard
Specificity ≥82.5%
clearances.comparator: Dilated fundus exam by retinal specialist
clearances.special_pathway: De Novo — no predicate existed for autonomous AI diagnostic at time of submission
clearances.key_insight: First autonomous AI diagnostic cleared by FDA. Set precedent that AI diagnostics do NOT require RCT — prospective single-arm with pre-specified performance thresholds is sufficient for De Novo clearance.

clearances.indication: AI-guided cardiac ultrasound acquisition guidance for non-expert users
clearances.trial_design: Prospective non-randomized observational study: non-expert users with vs without AI guidance
primary_endpoints: Diagnostic image acquisition rate by novice users with AI guidance vs without
clearances.comparator: Novice users without AI guidance (within-subject crossover)
clearances.key_insight: FDA cleared an AI imaging guidance tool with a prospective non-randomized within-subject crossover design — no separate RCT control group needed. The comparison was within the same user, not a randomized trial.

clearances.indication: AI-based detection of large vessel occlusion (LVO) in CT angiography for stroke triage
clearances.trial_design: Multi-site retrospective reader study on de-identified CTA images
primary_endpoints: Sensitivity and specificity vs. neuroradiologist read
Time-to-treatment metrics (real-world post-market data)
clearances.comparator: Expert neuroradiologist interpretation as ground truth
clearances.key_insight: FDA cleared a stroke triage AI using RETROSPECTIVE CTA data — no prospective study required for clearance. Real-world time-to-treatment benefit was demonstrated post-clearance in registry data, not in a pre-clearance RCT.

clearances.indication: AI-based detection of prostate cancer in H&E pathology slides
clearances.trial_design: Multi-reader multi-case (MRMC) retrospective reader study — pathologists with and without AI assistance
primary_endpoints: Reader sensitivity improvement with AI vs without AI
False negative rate reduction
clearances.comparator: Same pathologist reads without AI (within-reader comparison)
clearances.key_insight: First AI-based pathology tool to receive De Novo clearance for cancer detection. FDA accepted a retrospective MRMC reader study — no prospective collection needed, no RCT. The key is demonstrating reader performance improvement on a pre-specified holdout dataset.

clearances.product_name: Eko DUO ECG + Digital Stethoscope with AI
clearances.indication: AI detection of abnormal heart rhythms and cardiac murmurs in primary care
clearances.trial_design: Retrospective clinical validation on de-identified PCG/ECG recordings
primary_endpoints: Sensitivity and specificity for murmur detection vs cardiologist auscultation
clearances.comparator: Expert cardiologist assessment + echocardiography confirmation
clearances.key_insight: 510(k) clearance for AI-powered auscultation tool using pure retrospective validation. No prospective study required; substantial equivalence to predicate cleared this device. Retrospective datasets are accepted for 510(k) when pre-specified test sets are used.

clearances.indication: Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) for diabetes management
clearances.trial_design: Prospective accuracy study vs. YSI reference at-home and in-clinic settings
primary_endpoints: Mean absolute relative difference (MARD) vs. YSI hexokinase reference
MARD <10% across glucose ranges
clearances.comparator: YSI blood glucose reference (gold standard)
clearances.key_insight: CGM devices are cleared via prospective ACCURACY studies (MARD vs. reference), NOT via RCTs demonstrating clinical outcomes. The FDA pathway for novel CGM requires a prospective analytical performance study — no randomized trial of glucose management outcomes is required for clearance.

clearances.indication: Comprehensive genomic profiling (324-gene panel) for solid tumors as companion diagnostic
clearances.trial_design: Retrospective analytical validation on archived FFPE tumor specimens; clinical utility established from co-development with targeted therapies
primary_endpoints: Concordance with orthogonal reference methods (Sanger, IHC, FISH) for specific alterations
Analytical sensitivity and specificity per variant class
clearances.comparator: Orthogonal validated assays (Sanger sequencing, IHC, FISH) per alteration type
clearances.key_insight: FDA approved a 324-gene CGP panel using RETROSPECTIVE archived FFPE specimens — no prospective specimen collection was required. Clinical utility was co-established through partnership with co-cleared therapies (e.g., osimertinib for EGFR). This is the standard PMA pathway for comprehensive genomic profiling diagnostics.

clearances.indication: Liquid biopsy (cfDNA) detection of tumor mutations as companion diagnostic for NSCLC and colorectal cancer
clearances.trial_design: Prospective Specimen Collection, Retrospective Testing (PSRT) design — blood prospectively collected from ongoing therapy trials, then retrospectively analyzed with Guardant360
primary_endpoints: EGFR exon 19/21 positive percent agreement (PPA) and negative percent agreement (NPA) vs tissue biopsy
clearances.comparator: Concurrent tissue biopsy with validated EGFR testing assay
clearances.key_insight: FDA approved the first liquid biopsy CDx using the PSRT design — specimens were collected prospectively from real patients in the FLAURA trial, then tested retrospectively with the liquid biopsy. No separate prospective trial specifically for the diagnostic was conducted. This is now the standard approach for liquid biopsy CDx development.

clearances.indication: Companion diagnostic to identify non-small cell lung cancer patients eligible for atezolizumab
clearances.trial_design: Retrospective IHC validation on archived tumor specimens from IMpower110 trial patients; analytical validation on banked specimens
primary_endpoints: Technical concordance (TC ≥50% or IC ≥10% staining cutoffs) vs. reference labs
Association with clinical outcomes in co-approved therapy trial
clearances.comparator: Reference laboratory IHC protocols
clearances.key_insight: CDx approval using exclusively retrospective archived trial specimens. FDA accepted banked tumor tissue from the co-developed therapy's pivotal trial as the primary evidence — no separate prospective CDx trial was conducted. This is the standard approach for co-developed CDx: your validation specimens come from the drug trial's archived biobank.

clearances.product_name: WATCHMAN FLX Left Atrial Appendage Closure Device
clearances.indication: Prevention of stroke in non-valvular atrial fibrillation patients with CHA2DS2-VASc ≥2
clearances.trial_design: Single-arm prospective IDE study (PINNACLE FLX) with prespecified performance goals derived from prior RCT data (PROTECT AF, PREVAIL); prior generation used randomized IDE vs. warfarin control
primary_endpoints: Composite safety at 7 days (death, stroke, systemic embolism, device embolization, cardiac perforation)
Closure rate ≥98% at 12 months
clearances.comparator: Pre-specified performance goals (OPC) derived from PROTECT AF + PREVAIL meta-analysis
clearances.key_insight: FDA approved a next-generation cardiac device using a SINGLE-ARM study with performance goals (OPC methodology) — no head-to-head RCT vs. anticoagulation required for the WATCHMAN FLX. The original WATCHMAN (first generation) needed a randomized IDE trial (PROTECT AF); the FLX generation used accumulated clinical data as the OPC baseline.

clearances.indication: Remote hemodynamic monitoring of heart failure patients via wireless PA pressure sensor to guide therapy
clearances.trial_design: Prospective randomized IDE trial (CHAMPION) — single-blind, treatment vs. no-sensor control; 550 patients, 18 months
primary_endpoints: HF hospitalization rate at 6 months (primary)
All-cause mortality at 15 months
clearances.comparator: Control group (no sensor, standard care); clinicians blinded to sensor data in control group
clearances.key_insight: Class III cardiac monitoring device that DID require a randomized IDE trial — the CHAMPION trial. The FDA required randomized evidence because the intervention (changing therapy based on PA pressure) could cause harm if not effective. This is the exception for monitoring devices: when the device directly changes clinical management decisions, an RCT is more likely to be required than for pure measurement/diagnostic devices.

clearances.indication: Transcranial magnetic stimulation for major depressive disorder (MDD) — treatment-resistant
clearances.trial_design: Prospective randomized sham-controlled clinical trial (N=301), but subsequent expansions and next-generation devices used 510(k) substantial equivalence to cleared NeuroStar system
primary_endpoints: MADRS response rate at 6 weeks (TMS vs. sham)
Remission rate at 6 weeks
clearances.comparator: Sham TMS coil (blinded to patients, unblinded to technicians)
clearances.key_insight: Original TMS approval required a randomized sham-controlled trial for a novel neuromodulation device with no predicate. HOWEVER, subsequent TMS devices (figure-8 coil variants, helmet coil) cleared via 510(k) using NeuroStar as predicate — no new clinical trial required. This is the standard pattern: first-in-class neuromodulation needs RCT; subsequent 510(k)s only need predicate + analytical validation.

clearances.indication: Responsive neurostimulation (RNS) for drug-resistant focal-onset epilepsy
clearances.trial_design: Prospective randomized double-blind sham-controlled pivotal trial (RNS Pivotal Study), 191 patients, 12 weeks blinded period then open-label
primary_endpoints: % reduction in seizure frequency vs. sham (blinded period)
Responder rate (≥50% seizure reduction)
clearances.comparator: Sham stimulation (device implanted, no active stimulation)
clearances.key_insight: Class III brain stimulation device for epilepsy required a randomized sham-controlled PMA trial. The sham had the device implanted but inactive — this is the standard for implanted neuromodulation: a genuine control group where patients have the device but it's turned off. This is different from non-invasive neuromodulation (TMS) where sham is easier to achieve.

clearances.indication: Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) Type 1 in children under 2 years of age
clearances.trial_design: Single-arm open-label Phase 1/3 study (START trial), N=15 for pivotal cohort; natural history as external control
primary_endpoints: Achievement of motor milestones (sitting without support ≥30s) — no SMA Type 1 patient in natural history achieves this
Ventilator-free survival vs natural history
clearances.comparator: Natural history data from SMArtCARES and other registries (external control, not randomized)
clearances.key_insight: FDA approved a gene therapy for SMA Type 1 based on N=15 patients in a single-arm trial, with natural history as the external control — no placebo or sham group. The reasoning: sitting unassisted is virtually impossible in SMA Type 1 by natural history, so motor milestone achievement IS the proof of efficacy without a control arm. This demonstrates that for rare diseases with well-characterized natural history and large treatment effects, FDA accepts very small N, single-arm trials.

clearances.indication: Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA), all types
clearances.trial_design: Randomized double-blind sham-controlled trial (ENDEAR, N=121) for Type 1; randomized vs. sham for Type 2/3 (CHERISH, N=126); accelerated approval based on motor function improvement
primary_endpoints: Motor Milestone Response (ENDEAR): achievement of motor milestones assessed by HINE-2
HAMMERSMITH score improvement (CHERISH)
clearances.comparator: Sham lumbar puncture (intrathecal procedure, same positioning and needle insertion but no drug)
clearances.key_insight: Unlike Zolgensma (N=15 single-arm), nusinersen used a randomized sham-controlled trial even in Type 1 SMA. The sham involved an actual lumbar puncture procedure without drug delivery. This illustrates that FDA acceptance of single-arm trials in rare disease is case-by-case based on unambiguous effect size and natural history clarity — nusinersen's more modest effect size required a control group.

clearances.indication: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) amenable to exon 51 skipping
clearances.trial_design: Open-label 12-patient study + external natural history comparators; accelerated approval on surrogate (dystrophin increase by Western blot)
primary_endpoints: % increase in dystrophin protein level from baseline (surrogate endpoint)
6-minute walk test (supportive)
clearances.comparator: No placebo; comparison to historical natural history and external controls
clearances.key_insight: FDA approved a DMD drug based on N=12 patients with dystrophin production as a surrogate endpoint — over internal FDA review objection (4-3 commissioner override). This is the most extreme example of accelerated approval in rare disease: 12 patients, surrogate endpoint, controversial FDA decision. Confirmatory post-market trials were required. Demonstrates that surrogate biomarker endpoints CAN support accelerated approval in ultra-rare pediatric diseases with high unmet need.

clearances.indication: RPE65-mutation-associated retinal dystrophy (Leber's congenital amaurosis type 2)
clearances.trial_design: Prospective randomized controlled Phase 3 trial (N=31 total; 20 treated, 10 controls) — bilateral, sequential treatment; controls crossed over after 1 year
primary_endpoints: Change in Multi-Luminance Mobility Test (MLMT) bilateral score at 1 year (functional vision test)
Full-field stimulus testing (FST) as secondary
clearances.comparator: Untreated control group (crossed over after 1 year)
clearances.key_insight: FDA required a randomized controlled trial for a gene therapy even with N=31, because the natural history of the disease is variable (not uniformly poor like SMA Type 1). The key lesson: rare disease approval without a control group requires UNAMBIGUOUS natural history (universal disease progression). When natural history is variable (some patients have stable vision), a control group is needed even if N is very small.

clearances.indication: Robotic arm-assisted total knee arthroplasty (TKA)
clearances.trial_design: Substantial equivalence to cleared robotic surgical systems; 510(k) predicate pathway; clinical study not required for clearance
primary_endpoints: Substantial equivalence to predicate robot-assisted surgery systems (Mako partial knee system)
clearances.comparator: Predicate device — Mako partial knee system (K081001)
clearances.key_insight: A robotic surgical system for total knee replacement cleared via 510(k) substantial equivalence with NO clinical trial required. The safety and performance was demonstrated by equivalence to prior cleared devices, not by a head-to-head clinical trial vs. conventional TKA. Surgical robots with predicates do NOT require new clinical studies for 510(k) clearance.

clearances.indication: AI-based insulin therapy management decision support for type 1 diabetes patients
clearances.trial_design: Retrospective analysis of CGM and insulin pump data from a clinical study database; 10-fold cross-validation on de-identified records
primary_endpoints: HbA1c reduction vs. standard clinical recommendations (physician decisions)
Time-in-Range improvement at 3 months
clearances.comparator: Standard-of-care physician insulin dose recommendations on matched historical cohort
clearances.key_insight: AI insulin dosing decision support cleared via 510(k) using RETROSPECTIVE analysis of CGM/pump data from an existing dataset. The comparison was to physician decisions, not a randomized trial. FDA accepted retrospective validation for a CDS tool that provides insulin dose recommendations — demonstrating that even safety-sensitive CDS tools can use historical data for 510(k) clearance.

clearances.indication: Transcatheter mitral valve repair for symptomatic moderate-to-severe or severe degenerative mitral regurgitation
clearances.trial_design: Prospective randomized IDE trial (EVEREST II) vs. mitral valve surgery; 279 patients randomized 2:1 (device vs. surgery)
primary_endpoints: Freedom from composite: death, mitral valve surgery, or 3+/4+ MR at 12 months
clearances.comparator: Conventional mitral valve surgery (open-heart)
clearances.key_insight: Transcatheter structural heart device required a randomized IDE vs. open-heart surgery for first-in-class PMA clearance (EVEREST II). Later indications (functional MR: COAPT trial) were added via PMA supplement using a different RCT design. This shows that first-in-class structural heart interventions at high risk (requiring surgical comparator) DO need randomized IDE trials.

clearances.indication: Cloud-based AI for automated cardiac MRI analysis (ventricular volumes, ejection fraction)
clearances.trial_design: Retrospective validation on 100 CMR cases (expert-annotated); no prospective study required
primary_endpoints: Intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) vs. expert manual segmentation for LV/RV volumes and EF
Bland-Altman agreement analysis
clearances.comparator: Expert manual CMR segmentation as ground truth
clearances.key_insight: First cloud-based AI diagnostic cleared by FDA. Only 100 retrospective cases were needed to demonstrate agreement with expert segmentation. This is the minimal viable dataset for an AI imaging measurement tool: N=100 retrospective cases, ICC as primary metric. Subsequent similar tools have used even larger N for more complex tasks, but this set the floor.
